messages:
maya: Quick sync — we need to lock span/attr conventions for LLM requests today so exporters/alerts don't keep drifting. Current doc has mixed prefixes (llm.*, redwood.*). Any strong opinions?
liam: I'd prefer a single company prefix to avoid collisions: `redwood.llm.*` for platform-specific attrs, and stick to `llm.*` only for upstream generic semantic conventions.
ashley: +1 on company prefix for platform-only props. But we should be careful not to bloat span.name. Keep span.name semantic (e.g. `llm.generate`) and push metadata into attributes.
samir: I'm worried about downstream dashboards — we need cheap cardinality keys for grouping (model, route, policy) and high-cardinality attrs for everything else. Recommend: span.name = `llm.generate`, attributes: `redwood.model.id`, `redwood.route.id`, `redwood.routing.policy` and then token metrics as numeric attrs.
telemetry-bot: lint: span.name must be <= 100 chars. flagged 3 existing services.
eva: Also add a required attribute for `redwood.privacy.redacted` boolean when prompts are hashed/removed. We must never send raw prompt text to exporters.
liam: Proposed attribute set (example):
```
span.name = "llm.generate"
redwood.model.id = "redwood-3b-v2"
redwood.model.variant = "q4_0"
redwood.route.id = "public-api-v1"
redwood.routing.policy = "cost_preferred"
llm.input_tokens = 142
llm.output_tokens = 58
redwood.kv_cache.hit = true
redwood.request.batch_size = 4
redwood.privacy.redacted = true
```
maya: Question: should token counts use `llm.*` or `redwood.*`? We want token metrics to be queryable cross-platform (e.g., cost calculator) without company prefix.
ashley: Use `llm.input_tokens` & `llm.output_tokens` (generic), but add `redwood.tokens.estimate` for our internal billing adjustments. That keeps cross-compatibility.
samir: Another callout: we need `redwood.cache.source = "kv-cache"|"prefix-cache"` and `redwood.cache.key_source` to diagnose cache effectiveness. Also record `redwood.kv_cache.lookup_ms` for perf.
liam: Sampling & retention: keep 100% traces for errors and cold-starts, tail-sample for top latency decile, and otherwise 1% for normal traffic. Retention: full traces 30 days by default, aggregated metrics 365 days. Thoughts?
eva: Fine but compliance customers will need 90-day raw trace retention. Make retention configurable per org and per route.
maya: PII redaction: do NOT allow `prompt` or `user_message` attributes to be sent. If someone needs prompt-level evals, they must opt into a separate eval export that stores hashed prompt + test id.
telemetry-bot: action: created ticket INF-5423 to add redaction checks to agent and exporter.
ashley: Naming collision concern: avoid slashes in span.name that encode model. Instead use attributes for model. So `llm.generate` + `redwood.model.id` is canonical.
liam: For dashboards, create a derived metric `redwood.tokens.per_request = llm.input_tokens + llm.output_tokens` and export as gauge. That helps cost dashboards.
samir: One more: add `redwood.request.fallback_path` attr when routing falls back to older model or region. Examples: `fallback_to=cpu_variant` or `fallback_to=eu-region`.
eva: Can we add a small, consistent set of enum-ish attrs to keep cardinality low: `redwood.routing.policy` limited to {latency_preferred, cost_preferred, capacity_preferred, region_preferred}.
maya: ok action items: 1) adjust spec to use `span.name = llm.generate` + attributes prefixed as discussed, 2) enforce prompt redaction and add `redwood.privacy.redacted`, 3) sampling/retention defaults documented and org-configurable, 4) telemetry-bot ticket for exporter checks. I'll update the doc and ping infra.
liam: I'll make a small PR to telemetry spec with example spans + CI lint rules.
samir: I'll add metric export for tokens and cache hit ratio.
ashley: I'll stub dashboard templates (cost per model, token distribution, cache heatmap).
eva: :thumbsup:
maya: thanks — hearing no objections, moving to finalize.
